column2: Overnight Oats:  Tropical Sunrise (Mango, Coconut & Cashew)
Blend water and almonds together to a smooth milky consistency.  This is used in place of store brought almond milk
Then add 90% of the mango pulp and blend it all together.  Reserve the remaining mango pulp to drizzle on top before serving
Mix it with the oats and chia seeds to it and refrigerate overnight.  The liquid should be about twice the volume as the oats
in the morning the oats should have soaked the liquid and you should have a porridge consistency
Garnish with cashews, shredded coconut and mango pulp drizzle.  Serve with a side of blueberries and maple syrup
Soak: Rajma overnight.  Prep:  Chop onions.  Coarsely grind tomatoes.  Grind ginger garlic  green chilli into a paste.  Julienne ginger and chop cilantro for garnish
Boil : Add the required amount of water and salt and  boil the rajama until cooked properly.  If using a pressure cooker let it cook on slow flame
for 15 minutes after the cooker is at full pressure
Tempering : In a pan add oil.  When hot add jeera and saute until they crackle. Add coarsely ground green chilli, ginger and garlic paste and saute for a min
Saute onion with Tumeric poweder, corander poweder,  and salt  until the onions turn light brown
Saute for a few mins then add tomatoes and saute it until the mixture starts to leave oil on the sides
Drain the liquid from the cooked rajma and reserve on the side.  Add rajma (without the cooking water) and fry the beans with the masala
Then add the reserved water.  Let it simmer on low flame for 10-15 minutes. Add garam masala at the end and remove from flame.
Garnish it with Cilantro and ginger julienne
Green Salad with Sesame Ginger Dressing
Need gloves when making salad.  Make sure gloves dont get cut when chopping by knife or food processor
Dressing: simply blend the ingredients in vitamix until smooth. Add water as needed
The dressing should be of a creamy consistency and it thickens slightly with time
Wash and drain the lettuce and let it dry.  Cut the lettuce into bite sized pieces.  Thinly slice the cabbage and onions.
Cut the tomatoes, cucumbers and bell peppers into 1 inch cubes
In a large bowl, add everything except dressing.
Just before serving drizzle the dressing over the salad bowl. Use 2 wooden spoons and toss until everything is evenly coated.

Cut potatoes in 1/2 inch long wedges.  Cut the cauliflower into medium florets (1-1.5 inches).   Make a rough paste of ginger and green chillies. Slice Onion and cut in half.  Finely chopped tomatoes.
Heat the oil, once hot add jeera, turmeric.  Add ginger-chilly paste and onion and saute until onions are translucent. Add tomatoes and cook for a few mins.
Add turmeric, red chilly powder, coriander powder, salt and mix well

When tomatoes get cooked and oil seperates, dd potatoes and mix.  Cover and let it cook for a few minutes until the potatoes are about 50% done.  Add a splash of water to prevent potatoes from burning
Add cauliflower, salt and mix.  Cover and cook on medium-high flame turning it occassionally so that it doesnt burn
Add garam masala once the cauliflower and potato are cooked and give it a good mix.
Wash and soak the dal for 2 hours.  Boil on stovetop with 3x water and half the turmeric.  Keep stirring occassionally.  Remove from heat once fully cooked.
Finely chop the onions and tomatoes and keep aside.  Chop the cilantro.  Make green chilly-ginger paste.
Heat the oil, add whole red chilli, green chilli jeera, bay leaf, hing.  Add ginger and then add chopped onion.
Fry onion until translucent.  Add dry spices and mix.  Add chopped tomatoes and saute until the tomatoes are cooked and the mixture starts to release oil
Add the cooked dal to it and mix properly.  Let it simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes stirring occassionally
Switch off the flame, add lemon juice and garam masala and mix properly.  Garnish with cilantro before serving
Always use gloves when making food that will be served raw!  Wash cucumbers and dry.  Wash carrots and peel them
Slice both through the food processor.  Add salt and pepper.  Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve
Wash Toor dal and soak for 1-2 hours
Pressure Cook dal with turmeric and a little salt (1:3 water ratio) and then whisk it to mix it well
Take about 20% of the dal aside for vegan serving
For the regular dal:  bring the dal to a boil and make a seasoning with ghee, jeera, hing, red chillies.  Add to the dal and mix
Add lemon juice and chopped cilantro and switch off the flame
For vegan dal follow the same process but make the seasoning with oil instead of ghee
Heat oil. Add hing and cumin seeds. Add chopped green chilly and potatoes. Saute on medium flame. Cover.
Add salt, and continue to saute. Add a sprinkling of water (for it to cook faster).
Continue to saute and cover and cook - stirring intermittently - all on medium flame.
When potatoes are about half cooked add Coriander powder and chilly powder.
Continue to cook and stir. Again, add a bit of water if needed.
Add chopped coriander, frozen peas, and tomato.  Cover, cook, and saute till potatoes are done (should not be mushy)
Discard the top and bottom tip of the radishes and wash well
Peel their skins and grate them through a food processor (thicker shred)
Mix the grated radishes with salt, lime juice, and cilantro.  Serve
Wash the rice and mung dal and leave aside
Trim off the root end of the spinach bunch.  Wash by immersing in water, and removing it in a strainer
Chop the spinach in bite sized pieces
Heat the oil.  Once warm add cloves and cinnamon and allow them to sizzle.  Add jeera, hing, red chillies, and turmeric.
Add washed dal and saute for 4-5 minutes.  Add water and let it cook on open flame on medium heat (once boiling)
Add coriander and jeera powder, and salt and mix well
Once the rice and dal are cooked the consistency should be like a thick porridge, not dry.  Add water if needed
Finally add the lemon juice concentrate and spinach.  Mix well.  Cook until the spinach wilts slightly
Spinach should be bright green and not fully cooked.  Switch off the flame.  The remaining heat will cook the spinach
Serve with ghee on the side
In a bowl whisk together the gram flour (besan), green chilly-ginger paste, yogurt, and salt with water
Beat to a smooth mixture without any lumps.
In a saucepan heat ghee, add methi seeds, cumin seeds, cinnamon, cloves, hing, red chillies and curry leaves
Add the yogurt-water mixture which we had prepared earlier. Stir and mix well.
Bring it to a boil on medium-low to medium heat stirring occassionally so the mixture doesnt separate
Continue to simmer until the raw taste of besan is gone and the kadhi thickens.  Add sugar and mix till it dissolves
Garnish with chopped cilantro before serving
Finely chop cilantro, cut tomato, and cucumber in small cubes.  Grate the carrots in the food processor
Mix all the ingredients above, add salt, jeera powder, and lemon juice concentrate and mix well
Rinse the toor dal 2-3 times in water and soak it with 3x water and some hing and a few drops of oil for atleast 1-2 hours
Pressure cook it with turmeric.  Once the cooker is at full pressure reduce the heat and let it cook for 15 minutes
Switch off the flame and let the pressure drop naturally.  Once the pressure drops, open the lid and whisk the cooked dal together until its smooth
Soak the tamarind in hot water for an hour.  Make pulp and set aside
Chop the vegetables:  drumsticks into 2 inches long cuts, peel and cut taro root into 1 inch cubes, tomatoes into 1 inch cubes
Boil the vegetables in water with turmeric and salt.  Keet it covered and cooking at medium heat.  When half cooked add the tamarind water and half the sambar powder
Once the vegetables are soft, add the cooked dal, remaining sambar powder and salt.  Bring to a boil
Once it starts boiling lower the flame and let it simmer for 5 minutes.  You may leave the pot partially covered but stir occassionally and ensure the sambar doesnt boil over
Tempering:  Heat oil in a pan.  Once hot add mustard seeds, urad dal, jeera, methi, hing, dry red chillies and curry leaves
Add the tempering to the sambar.  Garnish with cilantro
Shred the cabbage in a food processor on the thick slice setting
Heat oil in a pot.  Add mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, few curry leaves and hing
Add shredded cabbage, turmeric and salt to taste.  Saute for 1-2 minutes
Cover and let it cook on low-medium heat stirring occasionally
Prepare the coconut masala by blending the coconut, kashmiri red chillies and jeera into a coarse paste (do not add any water - make this in the food processor)
if you are making the paste in the vitamix add a little water and make it in small batches
Add the coconut masala to the cabbage and mix well
Let it simmer for 2 minutes.  The cabbage should be cooked but should have a slight bite (dont overcook the cabbage)
Remove the frozen grated coconut from the freezer and let it thaw completely
Soak the mung dal for 1 hr and then drain the excess water, keep aside in a large mixing bowl. Do not soak dal for more than an hour.
Grate the carrots in the food processor and mix with the soaked dal
Clean and finely chop cilantro.  Finely chop green chillies and curry leaves and keep aside
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, once they sputter add urad dal, hing .  When urad dal is golden add curry leaves and green chillies
Add the coconut, salt, lemon juice, coriander leaves.   Toss and mix evenly and serve
Soak rice for 1/2 hour.  Soak the saffron in 25 ml warm water
Slice the onions, chop the tomatoes.  Cut the remaining vegetables in uniform sizes so they cook evenly.  Finely chop the herbs
Heat the oil, add whole spices and sliced onions and sautee until the onions are golden brown.  Add ginger, garlic and green chilly paste
Puree the tomato.  Add the tomato puree and half of the mint and cilantro to the onions and mix
Add kasuri methi, chopped vegetables, salt and mix. Also add the soaked saffron along with the water. Cover and let it cook on medium flame until the vegetables are about 80% cooked
Pour in 2 cans of coconut milk ( approx 4 cups) mixed with 4 cups of water, add remaining cilantro and mint and mix it well
Add soaked rice, cook on medium flame until water evaporates. Then cover with lid, lower the flame and cook for 15 minutes
Switch off the flame and let it sit for about 10 minutes before opening the lid
Finely chop onion and cilantro, cut tomato, and cucumber in small cubes
Mix all the ingredients above, add salt and jeera powder
Whisk yogurt and keep it on the side for people to help themselves.  Add a little salt and jeera powder to the yogurt.

column3: Blend water, almonds and chia seeds together to a smooth milky consistency
Add strawberries and blend pulse the mixture is pink.  Its okay to have a few pieces of unblended strawberry to add to the texture
Mix the blended mixture with the maple syrup. Add to the oats and give it a good mix
The liquid should be about about twice the volume as the oats.  Refrigerate overnight
in the morning the oats should have soaked the liquid and you should have a porridge consistency
Serve with a side of cashews, blueberries and maple syrup

column2: Wash & soak the chane in water overnight.
For the prep, add onion, garlic, ginger & green chilli in a chopper & chop it roughly, you don’t have to make it extremely fine, transfer the onion mixture into a bowl & chop the tomatoes similarly.
Discard the water from soaked chane & add them into a pressure cooker and cook it so that they are soft and not mushy.
Heat oil, once add the onion, garlic, ginger, green chilli chopped and saute for a bit.  Add tomato and saute until the oil starts to separate.
Add turmeric, coriander and jeera powder, garam masala, red chilli powder salt and let it cook well
Add the boiled black chana along with any reserve water
Let the mixture cook and blend well. Add reserved water to desired consistency.
Gravy should be thin for this recipe but you can adjust it according to your preference.
Finely chop onion and cilantro.  Cut tomato, and cucumber in small cubes.
Mix all the ingredients above, add salt and jeera powder
Whisk yogurt and keep it on the side for people to help themselves.  Add a little salt and jeera powder to the yogurt.
Spices mixed with a little bit of water:
For Masala Mixture:  In a bowl add water, turmeric powder, red chill powder, hing, jeera powder and mix everything properly then keep aside for further use
In a pot heat oil.  Add cumin seeds, ginger, green chillies, garlic and saute for a few seconds then add the prepared masala mixture
Saute until the oil starts separating. Add tomato and saute until cooked.  Then add cauliflower, potatoes, salt, water and mix everything properly.
Then cover and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes.
Remove the lid and stir in the chopped coriander leaves. Switch off the flames then cover and keep aside for 2-3 minutes.
Then garnish with chopped cilantro and serve
Wash and soak the dal for 2 hours.  Boil on stovetop with 3x water and half the turmeric.  Keep stirring occassionally.  Remove from heat once fully cooked.
Finely chop the onions and tomatoes and keep aside.  Chop the cilantro.  Make green chilly-ginger-garlic paste.
Heat the oil, add whole red chilli, green chilli jeera, bay leaf, hing.  Add ginger and then add chopped onion.
Fry onion until translucent.  Add dry spices and mix.  Add chopped tomatoes and saute until the tomatoes are cooked and the mixture starts to release oil
Add the cooked dal to it and mix properly.  Let it simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes stirring occassionally
Switch off the flame, add lemon juice, kasuri methi, and garam masala and mix properly.  Garnish with cilantro before serving
Trim the end of romaine lettuce, wash and let it drain to dry
Need gloves when making salad.  Make sure gloves dont get cut when chopping by knife or food processor
Discard the top and bottom tip of the carrots and peel them.  Trim cucumbers and wash well.
Thinly slice the cucumbers and carrots in the food processor.  Finely shred the purple cabbage
For the salad dressing:  blend all ingredients together into a smooth creamy dressing.  Add water to get the right consistency
Wash Toor dal and soak for 1-2 hours
Pressure Cook dal with turmeric and a little salt (1:3 water ratio) and then whisk it into a paste and keep it aside.
Heat oil – add mustard seeds, cumin seeds,  cloves, cinnamon, methi seeds, dried red chillies, hing
Add curry leaves, ginger paste, green chilli paste and saute well
Then add tomatoes, turmeric powder, coriander cumin powder, red chilli powder and cook till the tomatoes turn mushy
Add jaggery and tamarind paste.  Add cooked dal to this tempering
Add 4 cups of water and adjust the dal consistency as required. Add garam masala and aachar masala.
Boil it for sometime and garnish it with chopped cilantro
Slice the radishes and cucumber through the thin slicer in the food processor
Mix all the ingredients above, add salt and lemon juice concentrate
Trim and discard both ends of the beans.  Chop them into small pieces (~0.50 inches).  Peel and dice potatotes into .75 inch cubes
Heat the oil in a pot.  Add mustard seeds, asafoetida.  Add the chopped vegetables.
Now add the turmeric, red chilly powder, and salt and mix well.  Cover for 5-6 minutes.  Uncover and mix well.
Add little water and let it cook on low flame until the beans and potatoes are cooked and most of the water is absorbed. This may take about 30-45 mins to cook properly. Mix gently in between
Once the green beans and potatoes are cooked and tender, add the ground cumin and ground coriander.
Mix well and cook uncovered on medium heat to burn off most of the excess remaining liquid. Allow 30-45 mins to cook properly on low flame.
Add salt to taste and a small amount of freshly squeezed lemon juice.  Add lemon juice based on taste. Mix and garnish with finely chopped fresh cilantro.
Thai Red Curry  with Vegetables and Tofu
Chop the vegetables and tofu into bite sized pieces (Broccoli + cauliflower 1 inch florets, red bell pepper into 1 inch squares, tofu into 1 inch cubes)
To a large pot add the creamy part of half of the coconut milk and reduce the cocount milk until it starts to release oil
Add the curry paste and saute for a few minutes until fragrant.  Add broccoli and cauliflower and mix.
Once a bit tender, bamboo shoots and tofu.  Once cauliflower is about 70% done add the red bell pepper.
Add remaining coconut milk.  Simmer for a few minutes taking care that the red pepper is still crunchy to eat.
All vegetables should be cooked with a slight crunch and not mushy.  Switch off flame and add cilantro
Shred the cabbage into thin long pieces in the food processor.  Shred the lettuce into long thin strips
Roughly chop the cilantro and mint
Combine tamari, garlic, chillies, lemon, sugar, and salt and then toss well to create the dressing
In a bowl mix all the ingredients garnish with sesame seeds, cilantro and mint
Let it sit for about 20-30 minutes before serving
Soak toor dal for 3-4 hours in lukewarm water;  Do not over soak dal.  Pressure cook it until soft; mash / hand blend till smooth.
Add hot water to adjust consistency as needed.  Final consistency should be like sambar
Add turmeric powder, hing, salt and bring to a boil
Add lemon juice just before serving.  Serve on the rice with a teaspoon of ghee
Trim the ends of the plantains, peel the green layer.  Cut vertically and slice into quarters of .5 inch thickness.
Store the cut plantains in water solution of turmeric and salt.  Cut the onions into slices
Take a large pot and add the cut plantains and some of the turmeric salt water.  Cook over low flame until about 90% done
Coarsely grind in a food processor:  Coconut, jeera, green chillies, a hand full of curry leaves and salt
In a kadhai heat the oil.  When hot add chana dal, urad dal, mustard seeds.  Once the mustard seeds crackle add red chillies, hing and curry leaves
Add sliced onions and saute until the onions are translucent
Check if the plantains are mostly cooked and the water has been mostly evaporated.  Once they are add the oil seasoning to the plantains and give it a good mix
Add the ground coconut paste.  Mix well and add lemon juice concentrate.  Saute for 3-4 minutes until all flavors are incorporated.  Adjust for salt
Wash and peel the chayote squash.  Cut lengthwise and remove the seed
Grate with a large hole grater in the food processor.  Blend the green chillies
Heat oil in a pot.  Once hot add urad dal, mustard seeds, jeera, hing, curry leaves, green chillies
Add grated chayote squash and salt to taste.  Saute and let it cook for 2-3 minutes.  It will cook quickly
Remove from heat and let it cool.
Whisk yogurt and add to the choayote squash.  Mix properly and adjust salt to taste
Finely chop the cilantro and add to garnish the raita before serving
Rinse the rice 2-3 times until the water runs clear. Set aside.
In a large saucepan over medium-high heat, add the oil. Once hot, add the rice and stir to combine
Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the rice is lightly roasted all over (about 10 minutes).
Add tomato paste, garlic, and diced onion to the pan and saute for 3-4 minutes.   Add bouillion, salt, peas, jalapeno and Tone's cilantro lime mix
Add water (1.25x of the rice).  Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low and cook for about 20 minutes or until the water is completely absorbed.
Remove from heat and allow to rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
Soak black beans overnight and add a bit of salt and baking soda to the soaking solution.  Drain in the morning and wash once
Pressure cook the beans with bay leaves.  Once the pressure cook has its first whistle lower the flame to minimum and cook the beans for 45 minutes
Let the pressure drop normally.  Open the cooker and discard the bay leaves and take out extra liquid and store on the side
Heat a large sauté pan over medium heat with half the oil.  Once hot, add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook until the onion has softened and is golden
Add the garlic, jalapeño, cumin powder, mexican oregano and paprika.  Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the tomatoes and let it cook until the tomatoes are cooked properly and the liquid evaporates.  Add black pepper at this stage.
Add the black beans with some of liquid  and bring to a simmer until thickened and saucy. If it gets too thick, add the reserve water from the pressure cooker
Stir in the remaining olive oil, a squeeze of lime juice, and cilantro. Taste, and add salt/pepper or more lime juice to taste.
Final texture of the beans should be saucy, not dry, separate beans
Optional step:  boil the tomatoes and cool.  Take the peels off and use it for the salsa for more flavor.  Can also grill them instead
Chop the onions, garlic and jalapenos in a food processor.  Lightly pulse the tomatoes in the food processor separately.
Finely chop the cilantro.  Mix everything together in a bowl.  Add salt, pepper, lemon juice and mix
Refrigerate it for 30-45 minutes (or a few hours) before serving
Slice the avocados in half, remove the pit, and scoop into a mixing bowl.  Husk and chop the tomatillos.
Mash the avocado with a potato masher and make it as chunky or smooth as you'd like
Finely chop the onions and cut the tomatoes into small cubes
Add all ingredients EXCEPT the tomatoes and mix. Give it a taste test and add a pinch more salt or lime juice if needed.
Wash the lettuce and pat dry.  Cut into bite sized pieces and serve the lettuce and baby spinach mixed with the meal.
Rinse the toor dal 2-3 times in water and soak it with 3x water and some hing and a few drops of oil and soak for 2-4 hours
Pressure cook it:  once the pot is at full pressure reduce the heat and let it cookfor 15 minutes
Switch off the flame and let the pressure drop naturally
Once the pressure drops, open the lid and whisk the cooked dal together until its smooth
Slice onions into thin slices after cutting them in half. Chop the radish into thin rings.  Chop tomatoes into 1 inch cubes
Soak the tamarind in hot water for an hour.  Squeeze it with your hands and remove the pulp and set aside
Heat the oil in a pot.  Once hot add mustard seeds, jeera, methi, hing, turmeric, dry red chillies and curry leaves
Add the sliced onion and saute until translucent. Add the tomato and salt to taste
Saute until the tomato is cooked well.  Add the radish and saute
Add the sambar powder and salt and saute for 2-3 mins
Add the tamarind paste and let it cook on a low flame for 10 minutes
Add the cooked dal and mix.  Adjust salt and sambar powder if needed
Finely chop the cilantro and garnish just before serving
Peel the beetroot and cut off the base and top.  Cut it in 4 quarters.  Now grate all through a food processor thick blade.
Keep aside.  Slice onions and keep aside.  Make a coarse paste of coconut, green chillies and jeera
Take coconut oil in a pot.  Once hot add mustard seeds, once they splutter add curry leaves and turmeric powder
Add the grated beetroot and salt and give it a good mix.  Cover and let it cook on low flame for 2-3 minutes
Uncover and mix.  Add some water to help the beetroot cook well.  Cover and cook the beetroot well.  If it needs more water add some along the way
Once the beetroot is cooked you dont want any leftover water, so be careful to not add too much water
Add the ground coconut paste and give it a good mix.  Turn off the flame and cover and let it sit for 5 minutes
Shred the cabbage into thin long pieces, and finely chop the onion.  Thaw the coconut to room temperature.  Finely chop the cilantro
Mix together cabbage, onion, coconut, cilantro, lemon juice, salt and pepper
Heat up coconut oil in a pan.  Once hot add mustard seeds, jeera, hing and curry leaves and add the tempering to the salad
Mix it all up.  Garnish with some cilantro before serving
Wash the rice and dal and set aside for about an hour.  In a large pot combine the rice, dal and water.  Bring it to a boil
Add turmeric and black peppercorns and let it cook on medium flame.  Add salt once the khichdi is almost done and mix well
Keep stirring and add water if needed.  The final consistency should be a thick porridge like; not dry like Pulav
Leftover Veggies into stir-fry or salad
This is a buffer created to finish up whatever vegetables are left in the kitchen
Make a simple stir fry by chopping the vegetables and adding it to a simple tadka of oil, jeera, hing and salt.
Add a touch of turmeric powder and red chilly powder
If vegetables lend themselves to a salad then make a quick simple salad
In a pot, heat mustard oil, add cumin seeds, fennel seeds let it splutter well.
Add the asafoetida, crushed chillies & ginger saute for a minute.
Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander powder saute for a minute.
Add tomato and saute until fragrant. Then add the potatoes and mix it well.
Add water, salt to taste, and stir it once then put the lid on and cover and let it cook on low-medium flame until the potatoes are cooked
Remove the lid and with the help of a masher mash some of the potatoes and then boil it for a minute.
Finish it with little ghee and garnish with coriander leaves.
Wash the dal thoroughly with plenty of water. Soak the dal for 1 hour
Pressure cook the dal until soft and mash it until smooth. Add water to get desired consistency
Heat oil in a pan add black jeera, red chillies, green chilles, bay leaf, turmeric and add it to the whisked dal. Add salt.
Let the dal boil for 4-5 mins. Adjust dal consistency by adding more water.
Cut potatoes and pumpkin in 1.5 inch cubes
Cut sweet potatoes in 1 inch cubes
Cut cauliflower cabbage beans eggplant in 2 inch cubes
Heat oil and add dried red chillies, bay leaves, one green chilli, and panch phoron.
Add potatoes and sweet potatoes. Fry for 3 minutes
Next, add pumpkin. Fry for 3 minutes.
Add cauliflower and fry for 3 minutes
Then, add long beans, and fry for 3 minutes.
Add cabbage and eggplant. Keep stirring and frying
Add salt and turmeric. Cover the pan and keep cooking the vegetables on low heat, stirring occasionally (about 15 minutes or so
Add sugar, and continue cooking, covered, for another 10 minutes. The salt and sugar will draw water from the vegetables, and allow them to cook in their own juices
Finally, garnish with green chillies, chopped coriander leaves, bhaja masala. Cover and rest for a few minutes before serving.
Wash and dry cucumbers, tomatoes, lettuce and cilantro. Peel the cucumbers if they are waxy.
Cut cucumbers, tomatoes, lettuce into 1 inch bite sized cubes
Add  salt, pepper, olive oil, lemon juice and mix well
Rinse and wash the basmati rice thoroughly
Cut onion and carrots into 1 inch cubes. Cut green chilies obliquely into 2 pieces.
Heat oil and add pepper, cardamom, cloves, bay leaf, tsp fennel, and cinnamon and saute spices till it turns aromatic
Add green chilli, crushed ginger garlic and saute well
Add onion and saute till the onion softens slightly
Add peas and carrots along with mint,  salt and saute till the mint shrinks slightly
Pour in 2 cans of coconut milk ( approx 4 cups) mixed with 4 cups of water and mix it well
Once the milk comes to a rolling boil add basmati rice and mix gently
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, or until the rice is cooked well.
Fluff gently, and add cilantro. Mix gently. Let the rice sit for sometime before serving so that the flavor enhances.
Fine chop onions and tomatoes, slit chillies, cut veggies in 1/2 inch cubes
Make a fresh paste of green chillies, fennel and coconut
Heat oil, add bay leaf, cloves, jeera, cardamom untill aromatic
Add chopped onions and fry until translucent. Add ginger garlic and saute well
Add tomatoes and saute until it gets cooked well
Add turmeric powder, salt, chilli powder, garam masala and cilantro and saute for 2-3 mins
Add veggies and cook for 3- 5 mins until veggies get cooked
Add the ground coconut fennel paste and cook for 2-3 mins until the aromatic
Wash the chana properly 3-4 times and soak over night for at least 8 hours.  Pressure Cook the dal with 1:3 ratio of chana: water.
The chana should not get mushy. It was be firm but soft. If you press it between thumb and finger, it should mash easily
Heat the oil in a pan on medium heat. Once hot add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then add urad dal, hing and saute until light brown.
Add chopped green chilies, and curry leaves. Saute for 30-40 seconds
Add boiled, drained chana and salt. Mix well and cook for 2 minutes.  Add grated coconut, jeera powder and coriander powder mix and cook for a minute
PS: The water drained from cooked channa is very healthy. Please use it for something or share and drink as soup :-)
Cut Carrots and cucumbers in to 2 inches long strips and about half inch thick
Add salt, black pepper, and mix well
Crush the saffron lightly between your finger and soak it in milk and leave aside
In some ghee roast the cashews on medium low flame until golden brown and keep aside
Heat up some ghee in a pot and roast vermicelli on low to medium flame until golden brown.  keep aside
Bring the milk to a boil in a large pot, stirring occassionally.  Once boiling add the roasted vermicelli and mix properly
Cook on low flame until vermicelli softens
Add the sugar and mix well;  let it simmer until the payasam thickens.  Turn off the heat
Add the saffron mixture, cardamom, raosted cashews and mix
